1562	\begin{lemma}[Vanishing relations give constant rank]
1563	  \label{lem:presentation_rank_of_vanish}
1564	  \lean{Module.MatrixPresentation.rankAtStalk_eq_of_relMatrix_eq_zero}
1565	  \leanok
1566	  \uses{lem:presentation_iso_of_vanish}
1567	  If \(\psi = 0\), then the localization \(M_{\mathfrak p}\) is free of rank
1568	  \(e\) over \(R_{\mathfrak p}\) for every prime
1569	  \(\mathfrak p \subseteq R\).
1570	\end{lemma}
1571	
1572	\begin{proof}
1573	  \leanok
1574	  By \cref{lem:presentation_iso_of_vanish}, \(M \cong R^{\oplus e}\); a ring
1575	  with a prime ideal is nontrivial, so \(R^{\oplus e}\) has constant rank
1576	  \(e\) at every prime.
1577	\end{proof}
1578	
1579	\begin{theorem}[Flat everywhere-rank-\(e\) modules have vanishing relation
1580	  matrix]
1581	  \label{thm:entry_ideal_flat_vanish}
1582	  \lean{Module.MatrixPresentation.relMatrix_eq_zero_of_flat}
1583	  \leanok
1584	  \uses{def:matrix_presentation}
1585	  \source{nitsure-hilbert-quot}
1586	  Let \(M\) carry a matrix presentation \((\psi, \pi)\) by \(e\) generators.
1587	  If \(M\) is flat and \(M_{\mathfrak p}\) has rank \(e\) over
1588	  \(R_{\mathfrak p}\) for every prime \(\mathfrak p\), then \(\psi = 0\).
1589	  (This is the direction of Nitsure's local universal property left implicit
1590	  in the source: a surjection \(R^{\oplus e} \twoheadrightarrow M\) onto a
1591	  locally free module of everywhere-rank \(e\) has zero kernel.)
1592	\end{theorem}
1593	
1594	\begin{proof}
1595	  \leanok
1596	  \uses{lem:matrix_presentation_fp}
1597	  By \cref{lem:matrix_presentation_fp}, \(M\) is finitely presented, hence
1598	  --- being flat --- projective.  The surjection \(\pi\) therefore splits:
1599	  choose \(s : M \to R^{\oplus e}\) with \(\pi \circ s = \mathrm{id}\).
1600	  The splitting yields an isomorphism
1601	  \(R^{\oplus e} \cong M \times \ker \pi\), \(x \mapsto
1602	  (\pi x,\, x - s(\pi x))\), so \(K := \ker \pi\) is a direct summand of a
1603	  finite free module, hence itself finite projective (in particular flat).
1604	  Localizing at any prime \(\mathfrak p\) and counting ranks,
1605	  \(e = \operatorname{rk}_{\mathfrak p} R^{\oplus e}
1606	     = \operatorname{rk}_{\mathfrak p} M + \operatorname{rk}_{\mathfrak p} K
1607	     = e + \operatorname{rk}_{\mathfrak p} K\),
1608	  so \(K\) has rank \(0\) at every prime; a finite flat module of
1609	  everywhere-rank \(0\) is zero.  Hence
1610	  \(\operatorname{im} \psi = \ker \pi = 0\) by exactness, and every entry
1611	  \(\psi_{ij} = (\psi(\delta_j))_i\) vanishes.
1612	\end{proof}
1613	
1614	\begin{lemma}[Comparison of entry ideals]
1615	  \label{lem:entry_ideal_le}
1616	  \lean{Module.MatrixPresentation.entryIdeal_le_entryIdeal}
1617	  \leanok
1618	  \uses{def:entry_ideal}
1619	  If \((\psi, \pi)\) and \((\psi', \pi')\) are two matrix presentations of
1620	  \(M\) by \(e\) generators (with possibly different numbers of relations),
1621	  then \(I(\psi') \subseteq I(\psi)\).
1622	\end{lemma}
1623	
1624	\begin{proof}
1625	  \leanok
1626	  \uses{def:matrix_presentation_base_change, lem:entry_ideal_vanish,
1627	    lem:presentation_free_of_vanish, lem:presentation_rank_of_vanish,
1628	    thm:entry_ideal_flat_vanish}
1629	  Base change both presentations to \(A := R / I(\psi)\).  The entries of
1630	  \(\psi \otimes A\) vanish by construction
1631	  (\cref{lem:entry_ideal_vanish}), so by
1632	  \cref{lem:presentation_free_of_vanish,lem:presentation_rank_of_vanish}
1633	  the module \(A \otimes_R M\) is free (hence flat) of rank \(e\) at every
1634	  prime of \(A\).  Applying \cref{thm:entry_ideal_flat_vanish} to the
1635	  base-changed presentation \((\psi' \otimes A, \pi' \otimes A)\) gives
1636	  \(\psi' \otimes A = 0\), i.e.\ every entry of \(\psi'\) lies in
1637	  \(\ker(R \to R/I(\psi)) = I(\psi)\).
1638	\end{proof}
1639	
1640	\begin{theorem}[Presentation-independence of the entry ideal]
1641	  \label{thm:entry_ideal_presentation_independent}
1642	  \lean{Module.MatrixPresentation.entryIdeal_eq}
1643	  \leanok
1644	  \uses{def:entry_ideal}
1645	  \source{nitsure-hilbert-quot}
1646	  Any two matrix presentations of \(M\) by \(e\) generators have the same
1647	  entry ideal.  (This is the presentation-independence of the Fitting ideal
1648	  \(\operatorname{Fitt}_{e-1}\), and is what lets the local entry-ideal
1649	  subschemes of \cref{lem:flat_locus_open} glue.)
1650	\end{theorem}
1651	
1652	\begin{proof}
1653	  \leanok
1654	  \uses{lem:entry_ideal_le}
1655	  Apply \cref{lem:entry_ideal_le} in both directions.
1656	\end{proof}
1657	
1658	\begin{definition}[Fiber rank]
1659	  \label{def:fiber_rank}
1660	  \lean{Ideal.fiberRank}
1661	  \leanok
1662	  \source{nitsure-hilbert-quot}
1663	  For a prime \(\mathfrak p \subseteq R\) with residue field
1664	  \(\kappa(\mathfrak p)\), the \emph{fiber rank} of \(M\) at
1665	  \(\mathfrak p\) is
1666	  \(\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)} \bigl(\kappa(\mathfrak p) \otimes_R M\bigr)\).
1667	\end{definition}
1668	
1669	\begin{theorem}[Point-set of the entry-ideal locus]
1670	  \label{thm:entry_ideal_prime_iff}
1671	  \lean{Module.MatrixPresentation.entryIdeal_le_prime_iff}
1672	  \leanok
1673	  \uses{def:entry_ideal, def:fiber_rank}
1674	  \source{nitsure-hilbert-quot}
1675	  Let \((\psi, \pi)\) be a matrix presentation of \(M\) by \(e\) generators
1676	  and \(\mathfrak p \subseteq R\) a prime.  Then
1677	  \(I(\psi) \subseteq \mathfrak p\) if and only if the fiber rank of \(M\)
1678	  at \(\mathfrak p\) equals \(e\).
1679	\end{theorem}
1680	
1681	\begin{proof}
1682	  \leanok
1683	  \uses{def:matrix_presentation_base_change, lem:entry_ideal_vanish,
1684	    lem:presentation_iso_of_vanish, thm:entry_ideal_flat_vanish}
1685	  Base change the presentation to the residue field
1686	  \(\kappa(\mathfrak p)\), whose structure map has kernel exactly
1687	  \(\mathfrak p\).  If \(I(\psi) \subseteq \mathfrak p\), the fiber
1688	  presentation has vanishing relation matrix
1689	  (\cref{lem:entry_ideal_vanish}), so the fiber is isomorphic to
1690	  \(\kappa(\mathfrak p)^{\oplus e}\)
1691	  (\cref{lem:presentation_iso_of_vanish}) and has dimension \(e\).
1692	  Conversely, if the fiber has dimension \(e\), then --- every module over
1693	  a field being free, and free modules over a field having rank equal to
1694	  their dimension at the unique relevant localization --- the fiber
1695	  presentation satisfies the hypotheses of
1696	  \cref{thm:entry_ideal_flat_vanish}, so its relation matrix vanishes and
1697	  every entry of \(\psi\) lies in
1698	  \(\ker(R \to \kappa(\mathfrak p)) = \mathfrak p\).
1699	\end{proof}
1700	
1701	\begin{theorem}[Nakayama prolongation of a fiber basis]
1702	  \label{thm:nakayama_prolongation}
1703	  \lean{Module.FinitePresentation.exists_matrixPresentation_of_isLocalizedModule}
1704	  \leanok
1705	  \uses{def:matrix_presentation, def:fiber_rank}
1706	  \source{nitsure-hilbert-quot}
1707	  Let \(M\) be finitely presented over \(R\), let \(\mathfrak p \subseteq R\)
1708	  be a prime, and let \(e\) be the fiber rank of \(M\) at \(\mathfrak p\).
1709	  Then there exists \(g \notin \mathfrak p\) such that every localization of
1710	  \(M\) away from \(g\) --- that is, every module \(N\) over an \(R\)-algebra
1711	  \(R'\) realizing the localizations of \(R\) and \(M\) at the powers of
1712	  \(g\) --- admits a matrix presentation by exactly \(e\) generators.
1713	\end{theorem}
1714	
1715	\begin{proof}
1716	  \leanok
1717	  \uses{lem:matrix_presentation_fp}
1718	  Every element of the fiber \(\kappa(\mathfrak p) \otimes_R M\) becomes,
1719	  after scaling by some \(r \notin \mathfrak p\) (a unit of
1720	  \(\kappa(\mathfrak p)\)), a pure tensor \(1 \otimes s\) with \(s \in M\):
1721	  this holds for pure tensors \(c \otimes s\) because
1722	  \(\kappa(\mathfrak p)\) is a localization of \(R/\mathfrak p\)-fractions
1723	  (clear the denominator of \(c\)), and sums are handled by scaling both
1724	  summands by the product of their two scalars.  Scaling each vector of a
1725	  basis of the fiber this way produces \(m_1, \dots, m_e \in M\) whose
1726	  images \(1 \otimes m_i\) again form a basis of the fiber (they differ from
1727	  the original basis by unit scalars).
1728	
1729	  Let \(\alpha : R^{\oplus e} \to M\) send the standard basis to the
1730	  \(m_i\), and let \(Q := M / \operatorname{im} \alpha\); it is finitely
1731	  generated.  Since the \(1 \otimes m_i\) span the fiber and the tensor
1732	  product is right exact, \(\kappa(\mathfrak p) \otimes_R Q = 0\); as
1733	  \(\kappa(\mathfrak p) \otimes_R Q\) is the fiber of the finite
1734	  \(R_{\mathfrak p}\)-module \(Q_{\mathfrak p}\) at the maximal ideal,
1735	  Nakayama gives \(Q_{\mathfrak p} = 0\).  Hence \(\mathfrak p\) lies
1736	  outside the support of the finite module \(Q\), which is the zero locus
1737	  of its annihilator, so there is \(g \in \operatorname{Ann}(Q)\) with
1738	  \(g \notin \mathfrak p\); thus \(g \cdot M \subseteq
1739	  \operatorname{im} \alpha\).
1740	
1741	  Now let \(R'\) and \(N\) realize the localizations of \(R\) and \(M\)
1742	  away from \(g\), with structure map \(l : M \to N\).  The images
1743	  \(l(m_i)\) generate \(N\) over \(R'\): any \(n \in N\) satisfies
1744	  \(g^k n = l(x)\) for some \(x \in M\) and some \(k\), the element
1745	  \(g x\) lies in \(\operatorname{im} \alpha\), and \(g\) and \(g^k\) are
1746	  units in \(R'\).  This gives a surjection
1747	  \(\alpha' : R'^{\oplus e} \to N\).  Localization is a base change, so
1748	  \(N\) is finitely presented over \(R'\)
1749	  (\cref{lem:matrix_presentation_fp} for \(M\), transported along the base
1750	  change); hence \(\ker \alpha'\) is finitely generated, and any finite
1751	  generating family of \(\ker \alpha'\), arranged as the columns of a
1752	  matrix, completes \(\alpha'\) to a matrix presentation of \(N\) by \(e\)
1753	  generators.
1754	\end{proof}

1756	\section{Universal property of the strata}
1757	\label{sec:flatstrat_universal}
1758	
1759	\begin{theorem}
1760	
1761	\leanok
1762	[Universal property of the flat-locus stratification (case \(n = 0\))]
1763	  \label{thm:flattening_stratification_universal}
1764	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.flatLocusStratification_universal}
1765	  \uses{def:coherent_sheaf_flat}
1766	  \source{nitsure-hilbert-quot}
1767	  Let \(S\) be a noetherian scheme and \(\F\) a coherent \(\OO_S\)-module.
1768	  Then there exist a finite index set \(I\) and locally-closed immersions
1769	  \(\iota_f : S_f \to S\) (\(f \in I\)) with pairwise disjoint images
1770	  set-theoretically covering \(|S|\), such that the pullback of \(\F\)
1771	  along \(\iota_f\) is flat over \(S_f\) for every \(f\) (in the sense of
1772	  \cref{def:coherent_sheaf_flat}), and such that, writing
1773	  \(S' := \coprod_{f \in I} S_f\) and \(i : S' \to S\) for the morphism
1774	  assembled from the \(\iota_f\), the pair \((S', i)\) has the universal
1775	  property: every morphism \(\varphi : T \to S\) for which
1776	  \(\varphi^* \F\) is flat over \(T\) factors \emph{uniquely} through
1777	  \(i\).
1778	
1779	  This is part (ii) of Nitsure's flattening-stratification theorem in the
1780	  special case \(n = 0\), stated with flatness in place of local freeness of
1781	  constant rank: for a finitely presented module the two notions agree
1782	  locally, the rank decomposing \(T\) into clopen pieces.  Nitsure states an
1783	  ``if and only if''; the converse direction --- any morphism factoring
1784	  through \(i\) has flat pullback --- is stability of flatness under base
1785	  change and is recorded separately once needed.  The universal property for
1786	  a relative family (Nitsure's part (ii) for \(\F\) on \(\PP^n_S\), hence
1787	  for projective \(\pi : X \to S\)) additionally requires the
1788	  cohomology-and-base-change layer of \cref{lem:noetherian_induction_strata}
1789	  and is not stated separately here; for a general \emph{proper} family the
1790	  universal property is not asserted by any source in the reference library,
1791	  and the reduced strata of \cref{lem:flat_locus_reduction_lean} do not
1792	  witness it (over \(S = \Spec k[\varepsilon]\) with \(\F = \OO_S\) flat,
1793	  the identity must factor through the stratification, forcing the canonical
1794	  non-reduced stratum structure).
1795	\end{theorem}
1796	
1797	\begin{proof}
1798	  \uses{lem:flat_locus_open}
1799	  By the case \(n = 0\) of the flattening stratification
1800	  (\cref{lem:flat_locus_open}), with its canonical scheme structure: locally
1801	  on \(S\), a basis of \(\F \otimes \kappa(s)\) prolongs by Nakayama to a
1802	  right-exact presentation
1803	  \(\OO_V^{\oplus m} \xrightarrow{\psi} \OO_V^{\oplus e} \to \F|_V \to 0\)
1804	  on a neighbourhood \(V\) of \(s\), and the closed subscheme
1805	  \(V_e \subseteq V\) cut out by the ideal of matrix entries of \(\psi\)
1806	  represents the locus where \(\F\) becomes locally free of rank \(e\):
1807	  for \(f : T \to V\) the pulled-back presentation stays right-exact, so
1808	  \(f^*\F\) is locally free of rank \(e\) if and only if \(f^*\psi = 0\),
1809	  if and only if \(f\) factors through \(V_e\).  The local strata glue by
1810	  this representing property into locally-closed subschemes
1811	  \(S_e \subseteq S\) with \(|S_e|\) the rank-\(e\) locus; the family is
1812	  finite because the fibre rank of a coherent module is bounded on a
1813	  noetherian scheme, and the images are disjoint and cover \(|S|\) since
1814	  every point has a well-defined fibre rank.
1815	
1816	  For the universal property, let \(\varphi : T \to S\) have
1817	  \(\varphi^*\F\) flat over \(T\).  A finitely presented flat module is
1818	  locally free, and its rank is locally constant, so \(T\) decomposes into
1819	  clopen pieces \(T_e\) on which \(\varphi^*\F\) is locally free of
1820	  constant rank \(e\); by the representing property each restriction
1821	  \(\varphi|_{T_e}\) factors uniquely through \(S_e\), and the
1822	  factorizations assemble to \(\varphi = i \circ \tilde\varphi\) with
1823	  \(\tilde\varphi : T \to \coprod_e S_e\).  Uniqueness: the strata have
1824	  disjoint images, so any factorization through \(i\) induces the same
1825	  decomposition of \(T\) into clopen preimages, and on each piece the
1826	  component through \(S_e\) is unique because \(\iota_e\) is an immersion,
1827	  hence a monomorphism.
1828	\end{proof}
1829	
1830	\section{Application: relative curves}
1831	\label{sec:flatstrat_curve_application}
1832	
1833	In the Route~A consumer setting, the input to the flattening-stratification
1834	machinery is the pullback \(C \times_k T \to T\) where \(C\) is a smooth proper
1835	curve over a field \(k\) and \(T\) is any \(k\)-scheme.  The hypotheses of
1836	Nitsure's \cref{thm:flattening_stratification_exists} demand
1837	\emph{projective} relative dimension, not merely \emph{proper}; we record that
1838	no extra work is required to instantiate the theorem in our setting.
1839	
1840	\begin{lemma}
1841	[Smooth proper curve over \(k\) is projective]
1842	  \label{lem:smooth_proper_curve_projective}
1843	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.TODO.smoothProperCurveProjective}
1844	  % SOURCE: [Hartshorne], II.6.7 / II.7.6 (curve \(\Rightarrow\) quasi-projective;
1845	  % proper \(\Rightarrow\) projective for curves), and standard consequences in
1846	  % chapter III. The precise statement ``every smooth proper curve over a field
1847	  % is projective'' is one of the classical equivalences for \(\dim 1\) and is
1848	  % textbook material; this block is project-bespoke (no verbatim source
1849	  % quote is reproduced here as the result is folklore-level and cited only
1850	  % structurally for the Route~A reduction).
1851	  \textit{Source: classical; cf.\ [Hartshorne], II.6.7 \& II.7.6 (curves).}
1852	  Let \(C\) be a smooth proper curve over a field \(k\).  Then \(C \to \Spec k\) is
1853	  projective.  Consequently, for any noetherian \(k\)-scheme \(T\), the relative
1854	  curve \(C \times_k T \to T\) is projective in the sense of Grothendieck (there
1855	  exists a relatively very ample line bundle on \(C \times_k T\) over \(T\)).
1856	\end{lemma}
1857	
1858	\begin{proof}
1859	  Projectivity of a smooth proper curve over a field is classical
1860	  ([Hartshorne], II.6.7 / II.7.6; alternatively: every divisor of large
1861	  positive degree on a smooth proper curve \(C\) is very ample, providing the
1862	  embedding \(C \hookrightarrow \PP^N_k\) for some \(N\)). Pulling the ample line
1863	  bundle back along \(C \times_k T \to C\) produces a relatively very ample line
1864	  bundle on \(C \times_k T\) over \(T\).
1865	\end{proof}
1866	
1867	\begin{corollary}
1868	
1869	\leanok
1870	[Flattening stratification for a coherent sheaf on a relative curve]
1871	  \label{cor:flattening_stratification_curve}
1872	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.flatteningStratification.ofCurve}
1873	  \uses{lem:smooth_proper_curve_projective, thm:flattening_stratification_exists}
1874	  Let \(k\) be a field, \(C\) a smooth proper curve over \(k\), and \(T\) a noetherian
1875	  \(k\)-scheme.  Let \(\F\) be a coherent sheaf on \(C \times_k T\). Then the
1876	  flattening-stratification conclusion of
1877	  \cref{thm:flattening_stratification_exists} applies: there is a finite
1878	  set \(I\) of Hilbert polynomials and locally-closed subschemes
1879	  \(T_f \hookrightarrow T\) for \(f \in I\), set-theoretically covering \(T\)
1880	  disjointly, such that (a) \(\F|_{C \times_k T_f}\) is flat over \(T_f\) for
1881	  each \(f\), and (b) any morphism \(\varphi : T' \to T\) such that
1882	  \(\varphi^* \F\) on \(C \times_k T'\) is \(T'\)-flat factors uniquely through some
1883	  \(T_f\).
1884	\end{corollary}
1885	
1886	\begin{proof}
1887	  
1888	  By \cref{lem:smooth_proper_curve_projective}, \(C \times_k T \to T\) is
1889	  projective, hence factors through a closed immersion into \(\PP^n_T\) for some
1890	  \(n \ge 0\).  Push \(\F\) forward along the closed immersion (extending by zero
1891	  outside the image) to a coherent sheaf \(\tilde \F\) on \(\PP^n_T\); this
1892	  operation preserves \(T\)-flatness in both directions because the closed
1893	  immersion is a finite morphism.  Apply
1894	  \cref{thm:flattening_stratification_exists} to \(\tilde \F\) on
1895	  \(\PP^n_T\) to obtain \(\{T_f\}\) with the stated universal property.
1896	\end{proof}

1431	\section{The entry ideal of a matrix presentation}
1432	\label{sec:entry_ideal}
1433	
1434	The rank strata of \cref{lem:flat_locus_open} carry a canonical --- in
1435	general non-reduced --- scheme structure, cut out locally by the ideal of
1436	entries of the relation matrix of a presentation.  This section develops the
1437	commutative-algebra substrate: presentations of a module by \(e\)
1438	generators, the entry ideal, its base-change behaviour, Nitsure's local
1439	universal property, independence of the chosen presentation, and the
1440	Nakayama prolongation producing \(e\)-generator presentations near a point
1441	of fiber rank \(e\).  Throughout, \(R\) is a commutative ring and \(M\) an
1442	\(R\)-module.

1432	\label{sec:entry_ideal}
1433	
1434	The rank strata of \cref{lem:flat_locus_open} carry a canonical --- in
1435	general non-reduced --- scheme structure, cut out locally by the ideal of
1436	entries of the relation matrix of a presentation.  This section develops the
1437	commutative-algebra substrate: presentations of a module by \(e\)
1438	generators, the entry ideal, its base-change behaviour, Nitsure's local
1439	universal property, independence of the chosen presentation, and the
1440	Nakayama prolongation producing \(e\)-generator presentations near a point
1441	of fiber rank \(e\).  Throughout, \(R\) is a commutative ring and \(M\) an
1442	\(R\)-module.

1420	\begin{proof}

\proof It is enough to prove the theorem for open subschemes of
$S$ which cover $S$, as
the resulting strata will then glue together by their universal property. 


\textbf{Special case: } Let $n=0$, so that $\PP^n_S=S$. 
For any $s\in S$, the \textbf{fiber} $\F|_s$ of $\F$ over $s$
will mean the pull-back of $\F$ to the subscheme
$\spec \kappa(s)$, where $\kappa(s)$ is the residue field at $s$. 
(This is obtained by tensoring the stalk of $\F$ at $s$ with the
residue field at $s$, both regarded as ${\mathcal O}_{S,s}$-modules.)
The Hilbert polynomial of the 
restriction of $\F$ to the fiber over $s$ is the degree $0$ 
polynomial $e \in \Q[\lambda]$, where $e = \dim_{\kappa(s)}\F|_s$. 

By Nakayama lemma, any basis of $\F|_s$ prolongs to a neighbourhood $U$ of $s$ 
to give a set of generators for $F|_U$. Repeating this argument,
we see that there exists a smaller neighbourhood $V$ of $s$ in which
there is a right-exact sequence
$${\mathcal O}_V^{\oplus m} \stackrel{\psi}{\to} {\mathcal O}_V^{\oplus e} 
\stackrel{\phi}{\to} \F \to 0$$
Let $I_e\subset {\mathcal O}_V$ be the ideal sheaf
formed by the entries of the $e\times m$ matrix
$(\psi_{i,j})$ of the homomorphism 
${\mathcal O}_V^{\oplus m} \stackrel{\psi}{\to} {\mathcal O}_V^{\oplus e}$. 
Let $V_e$ be the closed subscheme of $V$ defined by $I_e$. 
For any morphism of schemes
$f: T\to V$, the pull-back sequence 
$${\mathcal O}_T^{\oplus m} \stackrel{f^*\psi}{\to} {\mathcal O}_T^{\oplus e} 
\stackrel{f^*\phi}{\to}f^* \F \to 0$$
is exact, by right-exactness of tensor products. 
Hence the pull-back $f^*\F$ is a locally free ${\mathcal O}_T$-module of
rank $e$ if and only if $f^*\psi =0$, that is, 
$f$ factors via the subscheme $V_e\hra V$ defined by the vanishing of all
entries $\psi_{i,j}$.
Thus we have proved assertions \textbf{(i)} and \textbf{(ii)} of the theorem.


As the rank of the matrix $(\psi_{i,j})$ is lower semi-continuous,
it follows that the function $e$ is upper semi-continuous, which
proves the assertion \textbf{(iii)} of the theorem, completing its proof
when $n=0$. 


\textbf{General case: } We now allow the integer $n$ to be arbitrary.
The idea of the proof is as follows:  
We show the existence of a stratification
of $S$ which is a `g.c.d.' of the flattening
stratifications for direct images $\pi_*\F(i)$ for all $i \ge N$ for some
integer $N$ (where the flattening
stratifications for $\pi_*\F(i)$ exist by case $n=0$ which we have 
treated above). This is the desired flattening stratification of $\F$
